title: spec: ImportRowResultSchema declares an optional errors array (every failed cell of a row), so /import can report more than the first error (#25582 proposal 4)
body:
Filing gate: ③ maintainer-directed. The spec half of ruling `6377844879` (batch #9 item 3a, letter A, maintainer 2026-10-24T00:43:45Z) on #25582, proposal 4. Filed by the `domain:server` seat 1 under `cross-repo-coordination.md` rule 3, because the server lane holds no `packages/spec` (`lanes/server.md` red line). ⛔ Not a claim.
Business reason: an /import row with several bad cells reports only the first. The user fixes one cell, re-imports, and hits the next, once per cell (#25582: hotsrm's spreadsheet imports).
Reader: the `domain:spec` lane, `packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts`. The server half (`import-runner.ts`) rides #25582, which carries `Blocked-by:` this card.
Dedupe (open AND closed): "ImportRowResultSchema errors array every cell error of a row" → only #25582 and its closed predecessor #25493; no spec card.

## What to declare

`ImportRowResultSchema` (`packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts:401`) is a `z.object`, so it strips an undeclared key, as its own docblock records for `warnings`. Declare one optional member:

- `errors`: an array, one element per failed cell, `{ field, code, message }`. Present only on a failed row that has at least one cell error.
- The existing first-error keys `field`, `code` and `error` stay, and keep naming the first element, so every current reader is unchanged.
- Reuse an existing issue element shape if one fits (for example `ValidateDataIssueSchema`, which `warnings` already uses) rather than a new one. The spec seat measures which.

Producer: the core coercion already builds this list. `coerceRow` returns every error, and `import-runner.ts` (about `:1132`) keeps `errors[0]`.

## Out of scope
- Proposal 3 (`aliases` on options) is not ruled (letter A excludes it).
- The runner change: #25582's server half, after this lands.
